text: VBench is a comprehensive benchmark suite for video generative models. It decomposes “video generation quality” into multiple well-defined, hierarchical dimensions for fine-grained and objective evaluation, with a prompt suite, generated videos, an evaluation method suite, and human preference annotations. [@chk-53993f2dc5a3e6f49d46fe60] The abstract states that VBench dissects video generation quality into specific, hierarchical, and disentangled dimensions, each with tailored prompts and evaluation methods, and that it comprises 16 dimensions (for example subject identity inconsistency, motion smoothness, temporal flickering, and spatial relationship). [@chk-53993f2dc5a3e6f49d46fe60] Rather than a single-valued score, the authors break quality into 16 disentangled dimensions in a top-down manner, covering Video Quality and Video-Condition Consistency. [@chk-a2e18961ae5ae833903d46c5] They argue this comprehensive evaluation can inform future architectural and data choices. [@chk-ceb9a82c9b3c53bd0471d089]
